history.dynasty: Chaulukya (Solanki) patronage. Vimala Vasahi (1031 CE) was commissioned by Vimal Shah, minister of the Chaulukya king Bhima I of Gujarat; Luna Vasahi (1230 CE) was built by the brothers Vastupal and Tejpal, ministers of the Vaghela ruler; the Hastishala (elephant courtyard) was added in 1147-49 by Prithvipal, a descendant of Vimal Shah; the Pittalhar temple by Bhima Shah, a minister of Sultan Begada of Ahmedabad; the Parshvanath temple in 1459 by Mandlik and his family (verify individual attributions).
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - Jain (Shvetambara) temple complex; keep-or-drop decision needed for a Hindu-temples dataset. The five marble temples of Dilwara near Mount Abu - Vimala Vasahi, Luna Vasahi, Pittalhar, Parshvanath and Mahavir Swami - are celebrated as masterpieces of Jain temple architecture and one of the world's finest Jain pilgrimage sites. They are carved from white marble quarried at Arasoori Hill near Ambaji (~23 km from Abu Road, verify): the exteriors are deliberately plain while the interiors are extraordinarily ornate - carved ceilings (the Navchowki nine-ceiling series), pillars, arches, mandapas and domes, including Luna Vasahi's famous pendant-hung central dome with concentric bands of Tirthankara and monk figures. Built by Jain ministers of the Chaulukya/Solanki and Vaghela courts of Gujarat between the 11th and 13th centuries, with additions into the 15th century.

name: Dilwara Jain Temples
town: Mount Abu (CSV town 'Mount Abu (Dilwara)' normalized; the temples are at Dilwara village, ~2.5 km from Mount Abu town)
town_description: Mount Abu is Rajasthan's only hill station, in the Aravalli range of Sirohi district at about 1,219 m, built around the Nakki Lake with the Achalgarh fort nearby. Dilwara, roughly 2.5 km from the town, is the holiest Jain cluster in the region - a major Shvetambara pilgrimage centre that draws devotees and art historians from around the world, alongside Mount Abu's Hindu sites (Adhar Devi, Achaleshwar) and the Nakki Lake.

travel.airport: Maharana Pratap Airport, Dabok/Udaipur, about 165-185 km away (verify).
travel.railway: Abu Road station, about 28 km away (verify); taxis and buses connect to Mount Abu.
travel.road: Mount Abu is about 28 km uphill from Abu Road on NH-27 (verify); the Dilwara temples are about 2.5 km from Mount Abu town centre (verify), reachable by taxi or auto-rickshaw.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March. Widely cited tourist rule: non-Jain visitors are admitted only in the afternoon (commonly 12:00 PM - 6:00 PM - verify locally); dress modestly, and leather articles, cameras and mobile phones are restricted inside (verify).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Commonly cited as 12:00 PM - 6:00 PM for non-Jain visitors (verify); Jain devotees have separate worship hours. Confirm timings locally before visiting.
